activities.description: Sharan Burrow speaking about the challenges facing the world

scenes.contextualRelevance: Sharan Burrow implies that the current approach to globalization is not working and a new, more people-centered approach is needed.

narrativeProgression.description: Sharan Burrow outlines the numerous challenges the world faces
She briefly discusses the positive potential of technology and the World Economic Forum

scenes.thematicElements: Global challenges: displacement, xenophobia, misogyny, dictatorship, unemployment, inequality. Potential for positive change: Technology used for democratic purposes, building cooperatives, bringing people together through the World Economic Forum.
scenes.title: Scene 1

climax.description: Turning point when Sharan Burrow shifts from outlining problems to suggesting solutions.

storylines.description: Sharan Burrow discusses the challenges and potential solutions for a more equitable and just global future.

trimmingSuggestions.description: The World Economic Forum logo could be trimmed to a shorter duration.
The middle section where Sharan lists numerous problems could be shortened by summarizing some of the issues to prevent the scene from feeling repetitive and keep the audience engaged.

text_to_speech: if you think about the world we have today the challenges are just enormous we've got greater displacement of people than at any time in our history and yet the world's more center phobic re-emergence of misogyny that is just extraordinary has been unleashed by the kind of strong men mentality of of leadership around the world as we see emerging dictatorship even from democratically elected leaders unemployment still way too high lost generation of young people and 40% of mostly women and young people in an informal economic environment where they have no rights no minimum wage there's no social protection this is not a world that we want we don't want it for ourselves and we don't want it for our children and grandchildren I think there are some very very good examples of people using technology for democratic purposes to build cooperatives that you know you can call digital cooperatives if you like but we still have a whole range of conflicts that are really about vested interests and how we make money at any cost versus how we actually keep things in balance with people with their communities with our planet and indeed with a global economy it's not whether people are keeping up it's whether we are actually thoughtful about shaping a future where people matter people are at the center of it the World Economic Forum has generated a debate about technology the fourth Industrial Revolution is the framing it's given the real benefit of that debate is bringing people together across a whole range of institutions because we are as a people across all of our common interests and our communities actually working together to build the future we want

timecoded_text_to_speech.text: If you think about the world we have today, the challenges are just enormous.
We've got greater displacement of people than at any time in our history,
and yet the world's more xenophobic.
A re-emergence of misogyny that is just extraordinary has been unleashed by
the kind of strong men mentality of leadership around the world as we see
emerging dictatorship even from democratically elected leaders.
Unemployment is still way too high, lost generation of young people,
and 40% of mostly women and young people in an informal economic environment
where they have no rights, no minimum wage, there's no social protection.
There's not a world that we want.
We don't want it for ourselves and we don't want it for our children and
grandchildren. I think there are some very, very good examples of people using
technology for democratic purposes to build cooperatives that you know you can
call digital cooperatives if you like, but we still have a whole range of conflicts
that are really about vested interests and how we make money at any cost versus
how we actually keep things in balance with people, with their communities,
with our planet, and indeed with a global economy.
It's not whether people are keeping up, it's whether we are actually
thoughtful about shaping a future where people matter, people are at the centre of it.
The World Economic Forum has generated a debate about technology.
The fourth Industrial Revolution is the framing it's given.
The real benefit of that debate is bringing people together across a whole range of
institutions because we are as a people across all of our common interests
and our communities actually working together to build the future we want.
